findings.root_cause: The date-override success path returns before conflict detection runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the override as satisfying only the schedule-hours constraint, then continue to the existing `busy.every(...)` check instead of returning true.
findings.title: Date overrides bypass all busy-calendar checks
findings.trigger: A host has a date override containing the candidate slot and also has a booking, calendar event, booking-limit busy period, or other busy interval overlapping that slot.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 134 `return true;` exists verbatim in the patch. When `dateOverrideExist` is true, the function returns true immediately at line 134 without ever reaching the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153. This bypasses all busy-calendar conflict detection for slots within date overrides.

findings.body: The two separately constructed Dayjs objects never compare equal, so the unavailable override can admit the boundary slot.
findings.failure_mode: A zero-length marker for an unavailable date is not recognized.
findings.impact: The two separately constructed Dayjs objects never compare equal, so the unavailable override can admit the boundary slot.
findings.root_cause: Object identity comparison is used where timestamp equality is required.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare the timestamps with `.isSame(...)` or numeric `valueOf()` equality.
findings.title: Unavailable overrides use reference equality for Dayjs values
findings.trigger: A fixed host has an all-day-unavailable override represented by equal start and end times, and another round-robin host contributes a slot exactly at that time, such as midnight.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 114 `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` exists verbatim. Using `===` on two separately constructed Dayjs objects compares object references, not values, so this will never be true even when timestamps are equal. The unavailable-day marker check is broken.

findings.body: The fixed host is treated as available for time outside the override, so an invalid round-robin slot is exposed.
findings.failure_mode: Partially covered and end-boundary slots pass the override check.
findings.impact: The fixed host is treated as available for time outside the override, so an invalid round-robin slot is exposed.
findings.root_cause: The predicate tests whether ranges overlap rather than whether the entire event fits inside the availability range.
findings.suggested_fix: Require full containment: slot start must be at or after the override start and slot end must be at or before the override end, using a clearly defined end-exclusive boundary.
findings.title: Partial overlap is incorrectly accepted as full override availability
findings.trigger: A slot supplied by another host overlaps only part of a fixed host's override, such as a 09:30–10:30 slot against a 10:00–11:00 override, or starts exactly when the override ends.
findings.verifier_reason: Lines 118-123 exist verbatim. The logic checks if slotEndTime is before/same as override start OR slotStartTime is after override end to reject. This tests for non-overlap rather than full containment. A slot partially overlapping (e.g., 09:30-10:30 vs 10:00-11:00 override) would pass incorrectly.

findings.body: The callback finds another range that does not contain the slot and immediately rejects it; with disjoint ranges, valid slots can disappear from every range.
findings.failure_mode: One override range vetoes slots that are valid under another range on the same date.
findings.impact: The callback finds another range that does not contain the slot and immediately rejects it; with disjoint ranges, valid slots can disappear from every range.
findings.root_cause: The code searches for any non-containing override instead of searching for one containing override.
findings.suggested_fix: First collect overrides for the slot's calendar date, then accept when `.some(...)` range fully contains the slot; reject only when that dated collection exists and none contains it.
findings.title: Multiple date-override ranges reject valid slots
findings.trigger: A date has two disjoint availability ranges, such as 09:00–10:00 and 14:00–15:00, and a candidate is fully inside either range.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 106 `dateOverrides.find((date) => {` exists verbatim. The callback returns true when a slot is NOT within an override, causing `find` to return that override. With multiple disjoint overrides, a slot inside one will be outside another, triggering rejection via the `return false` at line 130.

findings.body: Every valid slot is outside at least one of the ranges, so `.find` returns that non-containing range and the slot is removed even when another range contains it.
findings.failure_mode: Schedules with split availability can lose all otherwise valid slots.
findings.impact: Every valid slot is outside at least one of the ranges, so `.find` returns that non-containing range and the slot is removed even when another range contains it.
findings.root_cause: The quantifier is inverted: the implementation looks for any range that excludes the slot rather than any range that includes it.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject only when no applicable working-hour range fully contains the slot, for example by using `!workingHours.some(range => range is on the day and contains the complete slot)`.
findings.title: Split working-hour ranges veto one another
findings.trigger: A host has multiple disjoint working ranges on the same weekday, such as 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 139 `workingHours.find((workingHour) => {` exists verbatim. The callback returns true when slot is outside a working hour range, causing `find` to return that range and trigger `return false`. With split ranges (e.g., 9-12 and 13-17), a slot in one range is outside the other, incorrectly rejecting it.

pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

This PR fixes that date overrides of fixed hosts are taken into account for round-robin events. This prevents round-robin events being booked where the fixed hosts are unavailable. 

This PR also fixes that date overrides didn't adjust to different timezones. If the organizer has a date override from 10-11 UTC it always showed the slots from 10-11 open no matter what timezone the attendee has.

Fixes #8207
Fixes #8329

Fixes: #8273

**Environment**: Staging(main branch) / Production

## Type of change

- Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How should this be tested?

**Date overrides for fixed hosts (round-robin):** 
- Create a round-robin event with one fixed host and host round-robin host
- Create a date override for fixed host (round-robin host should also be available at that time)
- Check available slots of event on the day of the date override, it should only show the slots where fixed host is available
- Test that with different time zones on booking page and on the availabilities of fixed and round-robin host

**Date override timezones issue:** 
- Create a date override 
- Go to the booking page of a personal event 
- Change the timezone to a different one that the availability with the date override is 
- See the available slots of the day with the date override change accordingly 
- Also test with different timezones here

raw_findings.failure_mode: An override stops governing slots after the UTC date changes.
raw_findings.impact: The override is not considered to exist for that portion of its interval, so the code falls back to recurring hours and can either expose unavailable time or hide override-only availability.
raw_findings.root_cause: Override applicability is determined from the UTC date of the override start rather than the organizer-local date or complete interval.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Associate overrides and slots by the organizer's local calendar date, or directly test each slot against the converted absolute override interval without requiring equal UTC date strings.
raw_findings.title: Override lookup fails when a local override spans UTC midnight

raw_findings.body: The floating UTC-encoded local time is interpreted as an absolute instant before obtaining the timezone offset, which can select the pre-transition offset and move the accepted override window by an hour.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Fixed-host availability is shifted by the DST offset difference on transition dates.
raw_findings.impact: The floating UTC-encoded local time is interpreted as an absolute instant before obtaining the timezone offset, which can select the pre-transition offset and move the accepted override window by an hour.
raw_findings.root_cause: A floating local date/time is treated as an already-real UTC timestamp when resolving its timezone offset.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Interpret the stored date and clock fields as local wall time in `organizerTimeZone` with `dayjs.tz(...)`, then convert that zoned value to UTC; do not obtain the offset by converting the pseudo-UTC `Date` as an instant.

raw_findings.trigger: A date override occurs after a daylight-saving transition on that local date, for example 03:30 on the spring-forward day in `America/New_York`.

raw_findings.trigger: A host has multiple disjoint working ranges on the same weekday, such as 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00.

raw_findings.body: Dayjs resolves an undefined timezone through its default/runtime timezone, producing environment-dependent and incorrect slot offsets instead of using the supplied organizer timezone.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Previously valid date-override inputs are converted using the server or browser timezone.
raw_findings.impact: Dayjs resolves an undefined timezone through its default/runtime timezone, producing environment-dependent and incorrect slot offsets instead of using the supplied organizer timezone.
raw_findings.root_cause: The implementation assumes an optional compatibility field is always populated.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `override.timeZone ?? organizerTimeZone`, or make the override timezone required and update every producer before relying on it.
raw_findings.title: Date-override timezone is optional but used without a fallback
raw_findings.trigger: An existing `getSlots` caller passes a date override containing only `start` and `end`, which remains valid because the newly added `TimeRange.timeZone` property is optional.

raw_findings.body: The organizer offset can be taken from the prior DST regime, shifting generated slots by an hour.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Date-override slots are generated at the wrong absolute time around DST changes.
raw_findings.impact: The organizer offset can be taken from the prior DST regime, shifting generated slots by an hour.
raw_findings.root_cause: The UTC-encoded wall-clock value is converted as if it were an absolute instant before its organizer timezone is applied.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Parse the stored date and time fields as wall time directly in the override timezone, convert that zoned instant to the invitee timezone, and derive both offsets from the resulting real instant.
raw_findings.title: Slot generation resolves DST from a pseudo-UTC timestamp
raw_findings.trigger: An override uses a local time after a DST transition on that date, such as 03:30 on a spring-forward day in `America/New_York`, and the invitee uses another timezone.

raw_findings.body: Only the converted hour and minute are retained, so the slot is attached to the currently processed day and can appear a full day late or early.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cross-timezone date overrides are generated on the wrong invitee day.
raw_findings.impact: Only the converted hour and minute are retained, so the slot is attached to the currently processed day and can appear a full day late or early.
raw_findings.root_cause: The conversion keeps the shifted clock fields but drops the shifted calendar date.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Convert each override to an absolute zoned interval and select the invitee day from the converted date as well as its clock time; do not reduce the converted value to minutes since midnight before handling day rollover.
raw_findings.title: Timezone conversion discards adjacent-day rollover
raw_findings.trigger: The organizer-to-invitee offset moves an override onto the previous or next invitee calendar day, such as an early-morning India override viewed in America/Los_Angeles.

raw_findings.body: The existing `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher iterates only over actual slots and does not compare array lengths, so this new regression test reports success despite missing availability.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Incomplete timezone-adjusted schedules are not detected by the regression test.
raw_findings.impact: The existing `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher iterates only over actual slots and does not compare array lengths, so this new regression test reports success despite missing availability.
raw_findings.root_cause: The added test relies on a matcher whose prefix comparison does not prove that every expected slot was returned.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the matcher to compare complete arrays or explicitly assert that the returned slot count equals the expected array length before comparing values.
raw_findings.title: The new timezone test can pass with missing trailing slots
raw_findings.trigger: The implementation returns only an initial prefix of the expected slots, for example just 08:30, while retaining the expected date key.

raw_findings.failure_mode: The primary fixed-host behavior changed by the patch can break without a failing test.
raw_findings.impact: CI does not verify the patch's fixed-host round-robin behavior, including that a fixed host's override constrains slots contributed by loose hosts.
raw_findings.root_cause: The only added scenario is a personal event with one user and does not exercise fixed-host filtering.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a round-robin scenario with one fixed host and one loose host, give the fixed host a date override narrower than the loose host's availability, and assert that only fully contained slots remain across attendee timezones.

When `dateOverrideExist` is true, the function returns true immediately at line 134 without ever reaching the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153. This bypasses all busy-calendar conflict detection for slots within date overrides.

validated_findings.body: The two separately constructed Dayjs objects never compare equal, so the unavailable override can admit the boundary slot.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A zero-length marker for an unavailable date is not recognized.
validated_findings.impact: The two separately constructed Dayjs objects never compare equal, so the unavailable override can admit the boundary slot.
validated_findings.root_cause: Object identity comparison is used where timestamp equality is required.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Compare the timestamps with `.isSame(...)` or numeric `valueOf()` equality.
validated_findings.title: Unavailable overrides use reference equality for Dayjs values
validated_findings.trigger: A fixed host has an all-day-unavailable override represented by equal start and end times, and another round-robin host contributes a slot exactly at that time, such as midnight.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 114 `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` exists verbatim. Using `===` on two separately constructed Dayjs objects compares object references, not values, so this will never be true even when timestamps are equal. The unavailable-day marker check is broken.

validated_findings.body: The fixed host is treated as available for time outside the override, so an invalid round-robin slot is exposed.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Partially covered and end-boundary slots pass the override check.
validated_findings.impact: The fixed host is treated as available for time outside the override, so an invalid round-robin slot is exposed.
validated_findings.root_cause: The predicate tests whether ranges overlap rather than whether the entire event fits inside the availability range.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Require full containment: slot start must be at or after the override start and slot end must be at or before the override end, using a clearly defined end-exclusive boundary.
validated_findings.title: Partial overlap is incorrectly accepted as full override availability
validated_findings.trigger: A slot supplied by another host overlaps only part of a fixed host's override, such as a 09:30–10:30 slot against a 10:00–11:00 override, or starts exactly when the override ends.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 118-123 exist verbatim. The logic checks if slotEndTime is before/same as override start OR slotStartTime is after override end to reject. This tests for non-overlap rather than full containment. A slot partially overlapping (e.g., 09:30-10:30 vs 10:00-11:00 override) would pass incorrectly.

validated_findings.body: The callback finds another range that does not contain the slot and immediately rejects it; with disjoint ranges, valid slots can disappear from every range.
validated_findings.failure_mode: One override range vetoes slots that are valid under another range on the same date.
validated_findings.impact: The callback finds another range that does not contain the slot and immediately rejects it; with disjoint ranges, valid slots can disappear from every range.
validated_findings.root_cause: The code searches for any non-containing override instead of searching for one containing override.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: First collect overrides for the slot's calendar date, then accept when `.some(...)` range fully contains the slot; reject only when that dated collection exists and none contains it.
validated_findings.title: Multiple date-override ranges reject valid slots
validated_findings.trigger: A date has two disjoint availability ranges, such as 09:00–10:00 and 14:00–15:00, and a candidate is fully inside either range.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 106 `dateOverrides.find((date) => {` exists verbatim. The callback returns true when a slot is NOT within an override, causing `find` to return that override. With multiple disjoint overrides, a slot inside one will be outside another, triggering rejection via the `return false` at line 130.

validated_findings.body: The override is not considered to exist for that portion of its interval, so the code falls back to recurring hours and can either expose unavailable time or hide override-only availability.
validated_findings.evidence:
dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") ===
        slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")
validated_findings.failure_mode: An override stops governing slots after the UTC date changes.
validated_findings.impact: The override is not considered to exist for that portion of its interval, so the code falls back to recurring hours and can either expose unavailable time or hide override-only availability.
validated_findings.root_cause: Override applicability is determined from the UTC date of the override start rather than the organizer-local date or complete interval.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Associate overrides and slots by the organizer's local calendar date, or directly test each slot against the converted absolute override interval without requiring equal UTC date strings.
validated_findings.title: Override lookup fails when a local override spans UTC midnight
validated_findings.trigger: An organizer's single local-day override maps to two UTC dates, which commonly occurs for long ranges in a non-UTC timezone, and the slot lies on the UTC date after the adjusted start date.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 110-111 exist verbatim. The date comparison uses the UTC date of the adjusted override start vs slot start. For overrides spanning UTC midnight in non-UTC timezones, slots on the second UTC date won't match the override's start date string, causing the override to be missed.

validated_findings.body: The floating UTC-encoded local time is interpreted as an absolute instant before obtaining the timezone offset, which can select the pre-transition offset and move the accepted override window by an hour.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Fixed-host availability is shifted by the DST offset difference on transition dates.
validated_findings.impact: The floating UTC-encoded local time is interpreted as an absolute instant before obtaining the timezone offset, which can select the pre-transition offset and move the accepted override window by an hour.
validated_findings.root_cause: A floating local date/time is treated as an already-real UTC timestamp when resolving its timezone offset.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Interpret the stored date and clock fields as local wall time in `organizerTimeZone` with `dayjs.tz(...)`, then convert that zoned value to UTC; do not obtain the offset by converting the pseudo-UTC `Date` as an instant.
validated_findings.title: DST transition overrides are converted using the wrong instant
validated_findings.trigger: A date override occurs after a daylight-saving transition on that local date, for example 03:30 on the spring-forward day in `America/New_York`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 107 `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()` exists verbatim. The `date.start` is a Date object interpreted as UTC instant, then `.tz()` gets the offset at that instant. For DST transitions, this may select the wrong offset if the stored time represents wall-clock time after the transition.

validated_findings.body: Every valid slot is outside at least one of the ranges, so `.find` returns that non-containing range and the slot is removed even when another range contains it.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Schedules with split availability can lose all otherwise valid slots.
validated_findings.impact: Every valid slot is outside at least one of the ranges, so `.find` returns that non-containing range and the slot is removed even when another range contains it.
validated_findings.root_cause: The quantifier is inverted: the implementation looks for any range that excludes the slot rather than any range that includes it.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Reject only when no applicable working-hour range fully contains the slot, for example by using `!workingHours.some(range => range is on the day and contains the complete slot)`.
validated_findings.title: Split working-hour ranges veto one another
validated_findings.trigger: A host has multiple disjoint working ranges on the same weekday, such as 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 139 `workingHours.find((workingHour) => {` exists verbatim. The callback returns true when slot is outside a working hour range, causing `find` to return that range and trigger `return false`. With split ranges (e.g., 9-12 and 13-17), a slot in one range is outside the other, incorrectly rejecting it.

validated_findings.body: Dayjs resolves an undefined timezone through its default/runtime timezone, producing environment-dependent and incorrect slot offsets instead of using the supplied organizer timezone.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Previously valid date-override inputs are converted using the server or browser timezone.
validated_findings.impact: Dayjs resolves an undefined timezone through its default/runtime timezone, producing environment-dependent and incorrect slot offsets instead of using the supplied organizer timezone.
validated_findings.root_cause: The implementation assumes an optional compatibility field is always populated.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use `override.timeZone ?? organizerTimeZone`, or make the override timezone required and update every producer before relying on it.
validated_findings.title: Date-override timezone is optional but used without a fallback
validated_findings.trigger: An existing `getSlots` caller passes a date override containing only `start` and `end`, which remains valid because the newly added `TimeRange.timeZone` property is optional.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 212 `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` exists verbatim. The `override.timeZone` property is accessed without fallback. If callers pass overrides without `timeZone` (it's optional per the type), `.tz(undefined)` uses dayjs default timezone, producing incorrect offsets.

validated_findings.body: The organizer offset can be taken from the prior DST regime, shifting generated slots by an hour.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Date-override slots are generated at the wrong absolute time around DST changes.
validated_findings.impact: The organizer offset can be taken from the prior DST regime, shifting generated slots by an hour.
validated_findings.root_cause: The UTC-encoded wall-clock value is converted as if it were an absolute instant before its organizer timezone is applied.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Parse the stored date and time fields as wall time directly in the override timezone, convert that zoned instant to the invitee timezone, and derive both offsets from the resulting real instant.
validated_findings.title: Slot generation resolves DST from a pseudo-UTC timestamp
validated_findings.trigger: An override uses a local time after a DST transition on that date, such as 03:30 on a spring-forward day in `America/New_York`, and the invitee uses another timezone.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Same root cause as candidate 5: both describe DST offset resolution issues from interpreting stored dates as UTC instants. Line 212 in slots.ts has the same pattern as line 107 in slots.ts. Same fix would address both.

validated_findings.body: Only the converted hour and minute are retained, so the slot is attached to the currently processed day and can appear a full day late or early.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Cross-timezone date overrides are generated on the wrong invitee day.
validated_findings.impact: Only the converted hour and minute are retained, so the slot is attached to the currently processed day and can appear a full day late or early.
validated_findings.root_cause: The conversion keeps the shifted clock fields but drops the shifted calendar date.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Convert each override to an absolute zoned interval and select the invitee day from the converted date as well as its clock time; do not reduce the converted value to minutes since midnight before handling day rollover.
validated_findings.title: Timezone conversion discards adjacent-day rollover
validated_findings.trigger: The organizer-to-invitee offset moves an override onto the previous or next invitee calendar day, such as an early-morning India override viewed in America/Los_Angeles.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 219-220 exist verbatim. The code extracts only hour and minute after timezone offset adjustment, discarding the date. When offset shifts the time to a different calendar day, the slot is attached to the wrong invitee day since only clock time is preserved.

validated_findings.body: The existing `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher iterates only over actual slots and does not compare array lengths, so this new regression test reports success despite missing availability.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Incomplete timezone-adjusted schedules are not detected by the regression test.
validated_findings.impact: The existing `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher iterates only over actual slots and does not compare array lengths, so this new regression test reports success despite missing availability.
validated_findings.root_cause: The added test relies on a matcher whose prefix comparison does not prove that every expected slot was returned.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Update the matcher to compare complete arrays or explicitly assert that the returned slot count equals the expected array length before comparing values.
validated_findings.title: The new timezone test can pass with missing trailing slots
validated_findings.trigger: The implementation returns only an initial prefix of the expected slots, for example just 08:30, while retaining the expected date key.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 800 exists verbatim in the test. The `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher (lines 53-58) uses `.every()` iterating over actual slots, checking if each matches expected. It doesn't verify array lengths match, so missing trailing slots won't fail the test.

validated_findings.body: CI does not verify the patch's fixed-host round-robin behavior, including that a fixed host's override constrains slots contributed by loose hosts.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The primary fixed-host behavior changed by the patch can break without a failing test.
validated_findings.impact: CI does not verify the patch's fixed-host round-robin behavior, including that a fixed host's override constrains slots contributed by loose hosts.
validated_findings.root_cause: The only added scenario is a personal event with one user and does not exercise fixed-host filtering.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a round-robin scenario with one fixed host and one loose host, give the fixed host a date override narrower than the loose host's availability, and assert that only fully contained slots remain across attendee timezones.
validated_findings.title: The fixed-host round-robin path has no regression test
validated_findings.trigger: The newly added `fixedHosts.every(...)` date-override logic changes or regresses while the personal-event timezone scenario continues to pass.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 788 exists verbatim. The added test uses a single-user personal event scenario. The patch adds `fixedHosts.every(...)` logic for round-robin filtering, but no test exercises this path with fixed vs loose hosts and date overrides.
